sentence: 396 A	Pt, ********, is a 10 day old female, diagnosed with double inlet left ventricle with severely hypoplastic right ventricle and hypoplastic aortic arch s/p hybrid procedure with bilateral PA banding, 4mm Goretex shunt, PDA stent, and bipolar epicardial pacer who is being referred by ******** ******* APRN for heart transplant Psychosocial Assessment.
Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt's parents and review of the medical records.
Living situation:  Pt's parents are currently living in a single wide ******* with an addition that they are renting from their pastor.
They have been there for about 2 months.
This home has well water and window air conditioning.
They use bottled water to drink.
They have no pets.
There is no smoking in the home.
Demographics:  Mother: ******* ******  DOB: **/**/****  Age: 30  Education:  High School Diploma (through ESE program with limited reading capability)  Employment:  Not currently employed.

Had been working at **** ****, and is able to return   Phone: ***-***-**** (cell)     Father: ****** ******  DOB: **/**/****  Age: 40  Education:  High School Diploma (through special program for emotional/ behavioral/ learning disability)  Employment:  ******* ******* *********, paid daily  Phone: ***-***-****     Siblings:  ****** ********* (half-brother/ mom's child)  DOB **/**/****  Sheltered with Ms ******** in 2017.
Healthy.     ******** **** ****** (half sister/ dad's child)  DOB **/**/****  (Resides with bio mother in **.
Born 11 weeks premature with hole in heart)     ****** ****** (half sister/ dad's child)  Age 7  (Resides with bio mother in **.

Healthy)        Additional support persons:     ******** ********, maternal great grandmother (***-***-****) Lives about 40 min from family and has custody of 5 yr old half-brother     ******* ***** (paternal grandmother) Lives about 1 hr away     **** ***** (paternal uncle) Lives about 10 min away with his 3 children      Support systems:  Parents are married.
They have been married for 2 yrs (**** **, ****).
They both have children from other relationships.
Mom has a 5 yr old son who currently lives with her grandmother, nearby.
He was placed with her in 2017 due to her having legal trouble and being incarcerated for 11 months on charges for methamphetamine.
Dad has 2 daughters, each by different mothers, who both reside with their mothers in Kentucky.
He also has had legal trouble related to marijuana and for pills that were not in their prescription bottles.
He is currently on probation.
He is also in legal trouble in Kentucky for not paying child support, and lost his driver's license as a result.
The family report that they have a lot of support from family and friends.
They disclosed that the maternal grandmother, who has the 5 yr old, is a big support.
They also state dad's mother and brother are nearby and able to assist.
In addition, they have a lot of support from their church family.
Currently, their pastor and the church family are assisting with funds towards their hotel stay.
In addition, they will be assisting with fundraising for the family towards the medical and displacement expenses for ********.
Mom has a valid driver's license and does all of the driving for them.
Dad states he is eligible to get his license reinstated after he pays the required fees ($750).
They have a truck they are currently using.
In addition, dad has a BMW that he is working to repair.
In addition, he has a ***** Impala which is currently in Kentucky.
The family identify as *********.
This church is assisting them with lodging and financial assistance, and is focused on helping them maintain sobriety.
The family denies any objections to blood products or transfusions.
Course of illness:        ******** was born with congenital heart defect that was NOT prenatally diagnosed.
Mom reports that she received prenatal care from ** *****.
She states that she had several ultrasounds, including one at 18 weeks gestation that included 'testing' to screen for potential birth defects.
She states they were never advised there was a problem until after birth.
Mom had an emergency C Section with her first pregnancy due to carrying beyond the due date and the baby becoming 'stuck' during induction of labor.
She was planned for repeat C Section for this pregnancy.
She delivered at ******* Hospital in ********.
Due to bradycardia and concerns for congenital heart defect, ******** was transferred to *** shortly after birth.
TMH did an echo that was concerning for DILV and possible pulmonary atresia.
She was then transferred to us for escalation of care.
She underwent hybrid procedure with bilateral PA banding, 4 mm Goretex shunt, PDA stent, and bipolar epicardial pacer.
She is being evaluated for heart transplant as well.
Financial Situation:     ******** is covered by Medicaid ******** insurance.
The family is interested in applying her for SSI.
In addition, the family is supported by dad's employment income.
He is paid daily.
He does not get paid for time off.
SW provided information on fundraising through ****.
Dad has already given this information to their church family for assistance with fundraising.
SW will also provide First Hand Foundation ***** application to assist with their travel and displacement expenses.
Family History:     There is some medical history in the family.
Dad's first child was born prematurely, with a hole in her heart.
He also had an uncle who died from a heart attack in his 40's.
Dad disclosed he has a testosterone deficiency.
Mom reports a history of asthma.
In addition, her mother has COPD (although she is a heavy smoker and drug user).
Both parents report a mental health history.
Mom has been diagnosed with depression and bipolar disorder.
She has been in counseling for this in the past.
She also reports post-****** depression with her first pregnancy.
She states she has had a few moments of being sad or overwhelmed since ******** was born.
However, she feels this is related to her medical condition.
Dad reports a history of anxiety.
He states he has previously been on Ativan, but is now on medical marijuana only.
Both parents have a significant history of drug abuse.
Dad is currently on probation for ********* and pain pills.
Mom has a history of methamphetamine, resulting in an 11 month sentence.
She states she also was required to complete a program.
She denies using since then.
However, meconium is positive for *********.
She states she quit using after learning she was pregnant.
Neither parent reports smoking.
However, dad disclosed he was formerly a 3 ppd smoker.
He states he quit 2 ½ yr ago.
Neither report any significant alcohol use.
Of note, mom's mother is a drug abuser and has served 18 months in prison for this.
Parents report she returned to drug use also immediately after release from prison.
There is history of DCF involvement as already documented, with older child being placed with maternal grandmother.
Mom states she still has legal rights for him, however.
She states she is eligible to have him reside with her again.
They state they are getting a room ready for him in the ******* they are now living in.
There is no reported history of domestic violence.
Adherence:  We do not have records of prenatal care.
However, parents report that they kept all appointments.
Dad verbalizes that he was the primary caregiver for his oldest child after her discharge from NICU.
He states he administered meds and feels comfortable that he will be able to do so for ******** as well.
There are concerns regarding parent's inability to read well and their apparent lower cognitive abilities.
Information that has been provided regarding transplant and post-transplant care has not been understood, per their report.
They will require extensive rooming in and adequate demonstration of needed skills prior to discharge.
This is true if ******** discharges with single ventricle protocol as well as if she needs to move forward with transplant.
Parents both express hope that she will not need a transplant.

Assessment and recommendations:     IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  2  Family Background & Social Support -  2  Financial/Insurance  - 2  Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 4  Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  3  Adherence - 2  Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  3  Health Literacy -  4  Coping Skills - 2     Total:  24 High Risk       The family scores as high risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.
Concerns include limited literacy and cognitive ability of both parents, history of significant substance abuse of both parents, and past DCF involvement.
Recommendations are listed below:     Recommendations:  *Provide ongoing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.
Use teachback method to confirm understanding and require demonstration of skills needed for care.
*Provide fundraising resources to assist the family with expenses that arise secondary to transplant   *Connect patient and family with counseling resources to assist with healthy coping strategies
